## The problem

Your chart is technically correct. The analysis behind it is sound. But nothing moves after you present it.

This tutorial explains why — and walks through exactly how to fix it using publicly available Nigerian immunisation data and R.

## What you will learn

-   Why chart titles are the most powerful design decision in any policy visual
-   How to reframe descriptive labels into decision-driving arguments
-   How to structure visual hierarchy so policymakers read your chart the way you intend
-   How to build and annotate policy-ready charts in R using ggplot2

## Prerequisites

-   R and RStudio installed
-   Basic familiarity with R
-   ggplot2 installed — if not run `install.packages("ggplot2")`

## The data

We will use publicly available immunisation coverage data from the Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (DHS). Register free at [dhsprogram.com](https://dhsprogram.com) to download it.
